instructions: Put the drumsticks in a large pot with 5 cups water and 1/2 tsp of the salt. Bring it to a boil, skim off any foam, then turn the heat to low, cover and simmer for 25 minutes. You're cooking the chicken to 175°F in the middle, so if you have a thermometer, check it there. No thermometer? Cut into the thickest part: it's done when the juices run clear.
Meanwhile, rinse the rice in a strainer until the water runs mostly clear, then let it drain. Drain and rinse the chickpeas.

Make the cacik. Grate the cucumber and squeeze out as much water as you can. That should be about 3/4 cup. Stir it into the yogurt with the garlic grated in, 2 tbsp chopped mint and 1/2 tsp of the salt. Chill it.
Transfer the drumsticks to a plate. Strain the broth. You need 3 1/2 cups for the rice.
Melt the butter with the olive oil in a second large pot over medium-low heat. Add the rice and stir for 3 minutes, until the grains turn opaque and smell toasty.
Add the chickpeas, 3 1/2 cups of the broth and the remaining 1 tsp salt. Bring it to a boil, then cover, turn the heat to low and cook for 15 minutes, until the broth is absorbed.
Take the pot off the heat. Lay a folded clean tea towel over the pot and put the lid on top. Let it rest for 10 minutes.
While the rice rests, pull the chicken off the bones in shreds and throw away the skin and bones. Moisten the chicken with a spoonful of the leftover broth.
Fluff the rice with a fork.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Spoon the rice onto plates and top with the chicken. Serve with the cacik.
method_notes: Carter's Cooking leads (no rating shown): chicken boiled for stock, rice toasted in butter and olive oil, chickpeas added, the rice cooked in the stock and rested under a tea towel, shredded chicken on top and cacik on the side. Lezzet and Ckbk agree on the toasted rice and the rest; neither shows a rating, so this is a fallback. It's plain rice with no orzo or vermicelli, which keeps it gluten-free.
